A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pistachio benchmark and generation pipeline. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original VAD evaluations in Table 2, VAU evaluations in Table 4, cross-dataset experiments in Table 7, and qualitative generation analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds cross-generator results, synthetic/real training experiments, and model-based annotation-quality assessments in Tables 3, 4 and S1.

M1.justification: V4 introduces a VLM Refiner that checks generated summaries against actual video content and corrects misalignments, extending v1's storyline-to-summary annotation procedure. The scene assignment, storyline construction and sequential Wan generation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V4 adds evaluation domains generated with Cosmos-2.5 and Hailuo-2.3, extending coverage beyond the original generator and retained real-video benchmarks. It also evaluates UCF-based Holmes-VAU annotations. Pistachio's original scene and anomaly coverage remains unchanged; the ten newly enumerated anomaly types were already represented in v1.

E2.justification: Fed-WSVAD joins the VAD baselines, and Holmes-VAU becomes an annotation-pipeline comparator. UCF-Crime-to-Pistachio and reverse comparisons now report CLIP-TSA and Fed-WSVAD; v1's corresponding VadCLIP and PEL4VAD entries disappear, although those methods remain in other transfer comparisons. The VAU model lineup is unchanged.

E3.justification: V4 introduces CLIP-TSA training conditions combining Pistachio with 10%, 30% and 50% of UCF-Crime, evaluated on UCF-Crime. Appendix A adds annotation consistency and richness scoring on a 1–10 scale using three LVLM evaluators. These are substantive new evaluation designs; the original benchmark splits and AUC/AP/F1 metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing alternative-generation examples and cross-dataset analyses, v4 tests generator dependence, the effect of mixing synthetic and real training data, and annotation consistency/richness against Holmes-VAU. These additions directly examine robustness, practical transfer and annotation quality.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional annotation evaluators provide separate model scores rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V4 adds Fed-WSVAD results, including 83.2% overall AUC and 71.9% AP, plus cross-generator, mixed-training and annotation-quality scores. Table 4 newly reports 83.96/24.25 AUC/AP for CLIP-TSA with Pistachio plus 10% UCF training data. Earlier VAD scores are retained apart from rounding, and VAU scores are unchanged. VadCLIP/PEL4VAD results for transfer between UCF and Pistachio are removed.

T1.justification: The scene-classification, anomaly-assignment and storyline equations, sequential video-generation formulation, and Algorithm 1 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new evaluations introduce no formal derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction moderates its dismissal of earlier VAU benchmarks: v1 says none provides practical or scalable evaluation, whereas v4 describes limited coverage that does not comprehensively capture VAU complexity. The central claims about a synthetic, balanced benchmark, automated generation and annotation-free VAU construction remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V4 substantially revises the VAD interpretation, emphasizing biological motion and Fed-WSVAD's semantic/federated mechanisms. It adds arguments about generator-independent representations, attributes poor UCF transfer to resolution and viewpoint differences, and interprets mixed training as evidence of complementary synthetic representations. Appendix A adds an annotation-quality interpretation. The general synthetic-to-real limitation was already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: V4 specifies VideoScore filtering of the bottom 5%, discloses manual VAD ground-truth labeling, names Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-VL-32B for aggregation/refinement, and adds feature-extraction references and a dataset/code access URL. These improve documentation without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. Hardware, generation time and existing prompt examples are largely retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds references for Fed-WSVAD, Cosmos-Reason1, Video-LLaVA, I3D and ViT. Holmes-VAU, already cited in v1, becomes a direct annotation-quality comparator. The related-work survey and broad positioning of controlled generation against existing VAD datasets remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the annotation procedure, implementation description and VAD discussion, with smaller introduction edits. Numbered method subsubsections become unnumbered headings, and the supplement adopts lettered sections. Most introductory, related-work, generation, VAU and concluding prose is retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column typesetting, substantially resizing and relocating figures, tables and the algorithm. V4 adds three experimental tables, restructures the statistics and transfer tables, and removes Table 1's camera-shot column. V1's standalone scene-ratio Figure 4 disappears, while its information remains in the retained supplementary distribution figure.

improvement.justification: V4 adds useful tests of generator dependence, mixed-data training and annotation quality that v1 lacked, while clarifying annotation construction and filtering. These provide a limited net improvement. However, new evaluation details remain incomplete, some transfer comparisons are removed, and the new cross-generator discussion misreports its table: the stated 85.22/82.34 AUCs do not match Table 3's corresponding CLIP-TSA values of 72.17/75.89. These weaknesses limit the reliability of the expanded conclusions and prevent a major improvement.
